entries.reason: an MPSImage operation encodes onto a command buffer, which the port's MTLCommandBuffer protocol does not vend (inert, 19 members undefined)
entries.effect: Neither of these two is a walk over an image. Both build a TRANSFORM - :249 "image transform (i.e. a cumulative distribution function of the histogram)" for the equalization - and their only encode is :425 encodeTransformToCommandBuffer:, which takes an MTLComputeCommandEncoder. That is the one thing this host cannot do at all: its AGX family lacks computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType: and the release's own kernel dies encoding. So there is no oracle here for a transform and no way to check an answer, and an untestable transform would be a guessed one. OWED until a host can run it.

entries.reason: MPSImageIntegral.h:31 annotates the class ios(9.0), and MPSImageIntegral.h:19-20 states the rectangle exactly: sumRect.origin = MPSUnaryImageKernel.offset, sumRect.size = dest_position - MPSUnaryImageKernel.clipRect.origin. The value at a destination position is therefore the sum of the source over that rectangle, which is a prefix sum this port computes on the CPU. The class declares no member of its own - MPSImageIntegral.h:33-35 is @end straight after the @interface - so the initializer is MPSUnaryImageKernel's and the encode is the object's, on MPSImage9.m. Measured 2026-09-30 on this host by tests/backports/host/mpsimage9/run.sh: 9 cases over 1x1, 3x2 and 5x5 images, 96 elements COMPARED 0 MISMATCHES, and both planted builds are caught (96/96 and 9/9). Every value is this port's own answer against a plain C reference written from the wording above, in the same process: host MPS cannot be the oracle here, this host's AGX family lacking computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType: and the release's own kernel dying on encode. No number on this row measures Apple's code
entries.effect: the sum of the source over the rectangle from the offset to the destination position, per channel, inclusive of the destination position itself - MPSImageIntegral.h:19-20 states the size as a difference of two POSITIONS rather than a count, so a rectangle that size holds one more sample per axis than its length. Computed in double through the walking layer (MPSImageWalk13.m) and stored at the destination's own element width. The kernel's offset is honoured as {0,0,0}, the header's default at MPSImageKernel.h:131-138; a caller who set a non-zero offset is answered against the origin and that path is owed MEASURED, and not against the release's own kernel: the oracle is a CPU reference in the port's own process, computed from the header formulas above, because this host's AGX family does not implement computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType: and the release's own MPSImage kernels die encoding. No number on this row is a measurement of Apple's code, and tests/backports/host/mpsimage9/run.sh is the harness: 96 elements, COMPARED 96 MISMATCHES 0, both planted builds caught

entries.reason: not a missing measurement but a placement the band machinery forbids. MPSImageResampling.h:122 annotates MPSImageLanczosScale ios(9.0) while :29 annotates ITS OWN BASE, MPSImageScale, ios(11.0) - a later base under an earlier class, which is the release's own hierarchy and not a mistake in this reading. Carrying LanczosScale in a 9.0 object would put a class that arrived at 11.0 into a 9.0 file, which is the mixed-release object the rules forbid, and MPSImageScale is itself an absent row of this family at 11.0, so the base cannot simply be written either. The filter is computable on the CPU - :110-121 names the Lanczos resampling algorithm, and a NULL scaleTransform means the source fits the destination exactly - so what is missing is the 11.0 base and with it a legal placement

entries.effect: Y = X / L^beta with L = delta + alpha/N * sum over q in Q(k) of X^2, NORMALIZED ACROSS NEARBY FEATURE CHANNELS with no spatial extent, per MPSCNNNormalization.h:379-387. The defaults are alpha 1.0, beta 5.0, delta 1.0 and kernelSize 5 (:397-413), all MEASURED on a fresh kernel; kernelSize is READONLY there, so the initialiser is its only setter. The divisor is the kernelSize and NOT the window's length: MEASURED with kernelSize 3 the implied divisor is 3.000000 at every output checked. Q(k) = [max(0, k-floor(N/2)), min(D-1, k+floor((N-1)/2))] is ASYMMETRIC, so with four channels and N=3 the first channel sees three and the last sees two

entries.reason: MPSCNNConvolution.h:1314 calls this class "a fully connected convolution layer a.k.a. Inner product" and :1316-1338 says the arithmetic is a convolution whose kernel spans the input, which is why this file has no convolution in it: the walk is MPSCNNConvolution's, this class's superclass, carried by MPSCNNConvolution10.m. The one initializer this object carries is the one the 10.0 surface has, :1376-1382's MPS_AVAILABLE_STARTING_BUT_DEPRECATED(ios(10.0, 11.0)) form, which takes kernelWeights as inputFeatureChannels * outputFeatureChannels * kernelHeight * kernelWidth floats laid out weight[outputChannels][kernelHeight][kernelWidth][inputFeatureChannels / groups] (:1364-1368) and biasTerms as outputFeatureMaps floats; both become the MTLBuffers MPSCNNConvolution reads them from, in shared storage because this port's MTLBuffer is host memory the CPU reads directly. entries.effect: the class is here and -initWithDevice: is refused by name (MPSCNNConvolution.h:1402 marks it unavailable). entries.effect: Y = pm + ps*(X - p0*M) / (delta + alpha*VAR)^beta per MPSCNNNormalization.h:139-142, over a CENTRED kw x kw window of one feature channel with the off-image value ZERO and VAR = E[x^2] - M^2. Every default is MEASURED on a fresh kernel and agrees with :151-178 to the digit: alpha 0.0, beta 0.5, delta 1/1024, p0 1.0, pm 0.0, ps 1.0. The header says alpha 0 is "not recommended and is preserved for backwards compatibility" and that with alpha 0 "it performs a local mean subtraction", which is what the measured top case is. p0 = 1 IS LOAD-BEARING and the measurement settles it: at alpha 0 the denominator is the constant delta^beta, so the release's answer solves M = X - Y*delta^beta, and at (0,0) that is 1.55555558 against the centred 3x3 mean 1.55555556. With p0 = 0 the answer at (0,0) would be 32 where the release answers -17.7777786

entries.effect: Y = X / (delta + alpha/(kw*kh) * N2)^beta per MPSCNNNormalization.h:26-28, where N2 is the sum of the squares of a CENTRED kw x kw window of ONE feature channel, the denominator divides by the window's AREA, and what falls outside the image is ZERO. The defaults are alpha 1.0, beta 5.0, delta 1.0 (:41-48), all three MEASURED on a fresh kernel. THE WINDOW IS CENTRED and that is measured, not read: at kw=3, where a centred window (first = -1) and a backward one (first = -2) are different windows, the release agrees with centred to 3.0e-06 and disagrees with backward by 7.7e+04. An earlier version of this row claimed an EVEN kernel's window reaches back, on the strength of a kw=2 case - and for a 2-wide kernel a centred window starts at -1 and a backward one at -1 as well, so that case could not tell the two rules apart and proved nothing; the claim is withdrawn and the kw=3 and kw=5 cases are what the row rests on

entries.reason: CARRIED, and the two measurements on this row are why no number in it is a measurement of Apple's code. The host's own MPSImagePyramid CRASHES on this encode: run against the system's own MPS on an 8x8 R32Float texture with four mip levels, encodeToCommandBuffer:inPlaceTexture:fallbackCopyAllocator: takes the process down with SIGSEGV, exit 139 (transcript .agent-work/runs/host/mpsr10/pyramid.txt, built and run by tests/backports/host/mpscnn10's sibling pyramid.m). The release therefore cannot be compared against here, and nothing in MPSImagePyramid10.m claims to match it. Seen from this port the same gap is that MPSImage13.m:253 makes every texture with mipmapped:NO, so there are no mip levels for such a fill to write into at all. That is why this class's encode is refused unless the caller's texture has the levels to write into, and refuses a texture with fewer than two. MEASURED 2026-10-01 on this host (Apple M4 Pro, macOS 27.0): every one of this slice's classes RESOLVES in the system's own MetalPerformanceShaders, and MPSCNNNeuronReLU encodes and writes - so the sentence this row used to carry, "host MPS cannot run here: this host's AGX family lacks computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType:", is FALSE here and the host's MPS is the oracle for every number below. MPSUnaryImageKernel9.m:111-116 refuses the in-place form by name on MPSUnaryImageKernel itself, for the MPSCopyAllocator reason; the one kernel over this class answers it in a category on its own class, because MPSImageConvolution.h:592-594 makes the in-place form this family's form and a subclass's own implementation is found before its superclass's.
entries.effect: the class is here, it carries no member of its own, and its in-place encode fills every mipmap level after the first: each is this class's inherited filter applied to the level above and then decimated to the level's own shape, which is what MPSImageConvolution.h:582-583 means by removing odd rows and columns. The levels are read and written through the texture's own -getBytes:...-mipmapLevel: and -replaceRegion:...-mipmapLevel:, which is what a pyramid is given - a texture, not an MPSImage. A pixel format this port carries no element width for, and a texture with fewer than two levels, are refused by name.

Below 10.0.1 and from 12.0 the weights are this port's and the walk runs as described above.

entries.reason: NOT 10.0 AS AN EXPORT, and the two measurements of this row differ on purpose. MPSImageConvolution.h:519 annotates this class ios(10.0) and the registry's own sdk-26.2-surface.tsv carries 10.0 for it, so this row's `introduced` field is what the SDK declares. tools/cache-index/first-rung.lua answers 10.0.1 for _OBJC_CLASS_$_MPSImagePyramid, and that is TRUE and answers a different question: first-rung measures whether a rung CARRIES a name, and this one carries it from 10.0.1 because MPSImageGaussianPyramid's super_class points at it. What an object is PLACED by is what a client can bind, and tools/release-split.lua - which measures what a rung EXPORTS, over the same held ladder - answers 16.0, which is what modules/apple/backports.lua's band() places an object by. MEASURED over the held armv7/armv7s rungs, the MPS* names each rung's export trie carries that contain "Pyramid": 10.0.1 and 11.0 export MPSImageGaussianPyramid and no MPSImagePyramid; 12.0 adds MPSImageLaplacianPyramid, +Add and +Subtract and still no MPSImagePyramid; 16.0 adds _OBJC_CLASS_$_MPSImagePyramid and _OBJC_METACLASS_$_MPSImagePyramid. So this class is MPSImagePyramid16.m's work, and sharing one .m with MPSImageGaussianPyramid (10.0.1) is the condition band() refuses with "an object carries API that arrived in one release, so split it" - measured, not argued.
entries.effect: the class is here with its three initializers - the default filter of MPSImageConvolution.h:505-506, the centre weight of :527-528, and the caller's own odd-sized kernel of :548-552 - and with the two properties :562-569 declares on it. It carries no encode: the header declares none on it and the kernels over it do. An even width or height and a missing weights pointer are refused by name, and -initWithCoder:device: is refused by name because the release's keys for a filter are in no header, so a decoder cannot rebuild them honestly. It is carried in MPSImagePyramid16.m because the ladder exports it from 16.0, while MPSImageGaussianPyramid is exported from 10.0.1 and the three Laplacian classes from 12.0. The name is an ALIAS through revenant_alias.h, because the release carries this class from 10.0.1 without exporting it: on a band below 10.0.1 the proxy IS the class and every member answers out of the state beside it; on 10.0.1 to 10.3.4 the release's own class answers, because attach.c gives it the five members it already has, and a pyramid built there carries the release's private weights, which no header declares and this port cannot read; from 16.0 the release exports the name and the band links neither this object nor the proxy, and no band of this machine reaches 16.0 - facts/MetalPerformanceShaders/Elements10.md, the pyramid family.

entries.effect: the Cholesky factorization MPSMatrixDecomposition.h:135-147 computes - A = L * L**T or A = U**T * U for a symmetric POSITIVE-DEFINITE matrix, written to the lower or the upper triangle as `lower` selects (:155-156, "If lower = YES the lower triangular part will be used"). Only the triangle is written: the header says L and U are TRIANGULAR (:141-143), so the other half of the result is not part of the factorization. A pivot that is not positive means the source is not positive definite and the answer is the header's own status at :40, NOT a square root of a negative number written as a NaN. The two triangles are ONE factorization mirrored rather than two implementations of it, and every read of an already-computed factor goes through the single mirror that stored it - measured 2026-10-01, a version whose mirror appeared at four index sites and disagreed with its own write left the upper triangle's inner products empty and the factor wrong on 8 of 9 elements. entries.reason: IMPLEMENTED, in MPSNNReduce12.m, and the walk is a CPU walk. What decides that the port could carry it at all is the release's own cache rather than the header: objc-inventory.lua over the 16.0 arm64e cache lists MPSNNReduceColumnMax in MPSNeuralNetwork with superclass MPSNNReduceUnary and 3 instance selectors, none of them an encode, so the walk is the one it INHERITS from MPSCNNKernel - and MPSCNNKernel is a class this port already carries (MPSCNNKernel10.m, cnn.json, introduced 10.0, implemented), whose own -encodeToCommandBuffer:sourceImage:destinationImage: walks the image on the CPU exactly as MPSCNNPooling10.m's and MPSCNNConvolution10.m's do. MPSNNReduce.h:201 carries MPS_CLASS_AVAILABLE_STARTING(macos(10.13.4), ios(11.3), macCatalyst(13.0), tvos(11.3)), whose ios() clause reads ios(11.3). The axis and the operation are the header's own per-class sentence and not this port's arithmetic. The read window is MPSNNReduce.h:31-42's clipRectSource, which "replaces the MPSCNNKernel offset parameter for this filter. The latter is ignored" and is INTERSECTED with the image, default MPSRectNoClip. The walk itself is the one MPSImageReduceUnary16.m already performs for the MPSImageReduce classes over the same RevenantMPSImageReadRegion / RevenantMPSImageLoad / RevenantMPSImageWriteRegion helpers, with the third axis MPSNNReduce names and MPSImageReduce does not added. Measured: 185 elements compared against a plain C reference written from the header's own wording, in the same process, with 0 mismatches; min, max and sum are compared for EQUALITY because they select or add values the source holds, and mean within one whole float32 ulp because it divides. Three mutations of this object - a column run starting at a row's stride, a feature-channel run walking pixels as well as channels, and the weight's default not being the header's 1.0 - each make the run red, so the comparison can fail. host MPS cannot run here, so no number on this row is a measurement of Apple's code: this host's AGX family lacks computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType: and the release's own kernel dies encoding with '-[AGXG16XFamilyCommandBuffer mtlnext computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType:]': unrecognized selector. What the rows say instead is the header's sentence, and the destination's SHAPE - which the header fixes the count of and never states - is the shape the count forces and is recorded as such rather than claimed as measured
entries.effect: the kernel is HERE and it computes: -encodeToCommandBuffer:sourceImage:destinationImage: walks the source on the CPU and writes the largest value of each column of each feature channel into the destination, so a caller that encodes gets numbers and not a texture. The count of answers is the header's own sentence - one per row, one per column, one per pixel - and the destination is that shape; where a row or column reduction carries the channel it reduced is decided from MPSCNNKernel's own sourceFeatureChannelOffset, since an MPSImage's row is a row of ONE feature channel, and that is stated here rather than claimed to be the release's measured layout. This class declares no `weight`: MPSNNReduce.h:413-420 puts the property on MPSNNReduceFeatureChannelsSum alone, and the release's own cache agrees - only that class among the twelve lists -weight and -setWeight: - so a weight has nothing to reach this walk through and the source's own values are what it combines. A destination too small for that count is refused BY NAME with the numbers in the message and nothing is written, because a write past the edge of a texture is what the release asserts on; the differential exercises it and the case prints the value that survived

entries.reason: IMPLEMENTED, in MPSNNStates12.m, and that file is where the ladder puts it: `printf 'MPSCNNNormalizationMeanAndVarianceState\n' | xmake l tools/cache-index/first-rung.lua` answers 12.0, the same rung its header's clause reads. MPSCNNBatchNormalization.h:102 annotates the class ios(12.0) and :103 makes it MPSState's, which MPSState11.m carries. Its two members are the mean and the variance, each an id<MTLBuffer> (:105 and :110), from an initializer that takes them and a class method that allocates one per feature channel. No number in this row is a measurement of Apple's code and this band claims none: the release's own MPS cannot run on this host (its AGX family lacks computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType:, so the release's own kernel dies encoding, which facts/MetalPerformanceShaders/Image9.md records). What was measured is in the facts page with the commands beside it: the armv7 build of this package's MPS directory (clang 23.1.1 -c -fobjc-arc -fvisibility=hidden -target armv7-apple-ios6.0 -isysroot the 16.4 iPhoneOS SDK -Wall over all 74 of its .m files, 0 failures) and ld -r -undefined dynamic_lookup over those 74 objects, which leaves no MPS class undefined - the only _OBJC_* symbols left open are ten framework classes (NSObject, NSArray, NSMutableArray, NSMutableData, NSNull, NSNumber, NSString, NSValue, NSObject's metaclass and MTLTextureDescriptor). That is a PARTIAL link over one directory and not a dylib link. No host case, no device run and no gate.
entries.effect: the class is here: -mean and -variance answer, -initWithMean:variance: holds the two buffers as strong ivars, and +temporaryStateWithCommandBuffer:numberOfFeatureChannels: makes two shared buffers of that many floats and puts both in MPSState's resource list, which is what makes the state answer -resource and -bufferSizeAtIndex: for them. What fills the two buffers is the batch normalization gradient, which is ios(11.3) and is another slice's object; this class allocates what the header says it allocates and the row does not claim a mean or a variance is computed.

entries.effect: the base carries the seven values every concrete optimizer reads, with the same defaults, and -setLearningRate: is the base's own (:265) because learningRate is readonly (:243). The gradient preprocessing every optimizer applies is this class's contract: clip to [gradientClipMin, gradientClipMax] when applyGradientClipping, multiply by gradientRescale, then add the regularization gradient - L1 the scale itself, L2 the scale times the weight - in that order. THE RULE IS THE HEADER'S, NOT A GUESS. MPSNNOptimizers.h writes each update out in full and each of the three formulas is transcribed here line for line: gradient descent at :250-268 (m[t] = momentumScale * m[t-1] + learningRate * g, variable -= m[t]; under Nesterov m[t] = momentumScale * m[t-1] + g and variable -= learningRate * (g + m[t] * momentumScale); with no momentum vector variable -= learningRate * g), RMSProp at :430-432 (s[t] = decay * s[t-1] + (1 - decay) * g^2, variable -= learningRate * g / (sqrt(s[t]) + epsilon)), Adam at :436-438 (t += 1, lr[t] = learningRate * sqrt(1 - beta2^t) / (1 - beta1^t), m[t] = beta1 * m[t-1] + (1 - beta1) * g, v[t] = beta2 * v[t-1] + (1 - beta2) * g^2, variable -= lr[t] * m[t] / (sqrt(v[t]) + epsilon)). The preprocessing is the header's order at :61-66 - clip, then gradientRescale, then the regularization gradient - and the two regularization gradients are its own at :33-41: L1 the scale itself, L2 the scale times the weight. Every default is the property's own doc: 1e-3 (:66), 1.0 (:72), NO (:78), 0.0 (:94), None (:100), momentum 0.0 (:253), decay 0.9 (:459), epsilon 1e-8 (:466), beta1 0.9 (:505), beta2 0.999 (:512), epsilon 1e-8 (:519). timeStep exists for the bias correction and the header increments it BEFORE lr[t] (:436), so the first update runs at t == 1. entries.effect: the source is resampled with a bilinear blend over the four pixels around each destination pixel, on the CPU, using MPSNNResize.h's own two conventions and no other: alignCorners == YES, which the header says preserves the values at the corner pixels, maps a destination pixel onto (source - 1) * x / (destination - 1); alignCorners == NO, the header's default, aligns the centres and maps them at (x + 0.5) * source / destination - 0.5. Both results are clamped into the source so no sample falls outside the image. The number of feature channels is unchanged, as the header requires, and a destination whose shape is not the one the kernel was asked for is refused rather than written at one shape and read at another. entries.effect: the class is here with its three initializers, its two coordinates and its fill. -encodeToCommandBuffer:sourceImage:destinationImage: writes the source into the destination with the pad on each side of each axis, one element at a time through the plane walk RevenantMPSCnn.h owns: an element inside the source's rectangle takes the source's own value and every other takes its channel's fill. entries.reason: the class is HERE and holds its own storage: an MPSNDArray is "a MTLBuffer based storage container for multi-dimensional data" whose major row is the 0th dimension (MPSCore/MPSNDArray.h's class discussion), and this port's device makes an MTLBuffer host memory the CPU reads and writes directly, so the array is one buffer, a byte offset and a descriptor, and the release's own accessors -readBytes:strideBytes: and -writeBytes:strideBytes: are strided walks over it. Four semantics the release's own answers settled and the header's prose alone got wrong here first, each measured in tests/backports/host/mpsndarray/run.sh and written into the facts page: the storage is PACKED and the 16-byte row is an ALLOCATION size, not an address (-resourceSize of a [2,3,4,5] float32 array answers 960 = 16 bytes a row over 3*4*5 rows while the element at (1,2,3,4) is at 1+2*2+3*6+4*24); -lengthOfDimension: on a descriptor reads THROUGH the permutation, so a transposed [2,3] answers 3 for dimension 0, while a transposed VIEW of a [2,3] array answers 2, the array's own shape, which MPSCore/MPSNDArray.h:235-237 permits; a slice changes the packed walk and not the shape, so a view of a [3,4,2] array sliced on dimension 1 reads its twelve values out of a view whose shape says twenty-four; and a nil strideBytes array means PACKED, which is a different number from the storage stride. A view is the parent's buffer with an offset and a permutation of the parent's strides and NO copy, which is the class discussion's "MPS will usually defer doing a physical transpose" and what -parent answers; MPSAliasingStrategyShallNotAlias is "Always make a copy" (MPSCoreTypes.h:329) and is honoured by materializing the view rather than ignored. What is measured against the RELEASE and what is not: an MPSNDArray is storage, so the substrate's shapes, views, strides and bytes are compared against the system's own MPSNDArray - tests/backports/host/mpsndarray/run.sh builds one case file twice and compares the two runs, 31 lines compared, MISMATCHES 0, both planted builds caught. A KERNEL's encode is not, and this host cannot be the oracle for one: its AGX family does not implement computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType: and the release's own MPS kernels die encoding, so the kernel cases are compared against a plain C reference written from the header's own wording and computed in the same process - 69 elements compared, 0 mismatches, both planted builds failing it. No number on a kernel row measures Apple's code.

entries.reason: the class is HERE and is what the header says it is - "A state created to record a MPSCNNKernel properties at the time an -encode call was made. The contents are opaque" (MPSNDArrayGradientState.h:17-23) - and it records the FORWARD kernel's filter and the sources' shapes, which is what a gradient pass reads. It adds no accessor of its own, because "the contents are opaque" and the only question a caller can ask of an MPSState is the one MPSState answers. Two properties the gradients NEED come from it, and both were wrong here first, which is why they are recorded: the gather's AXIS, which is a property of the forward kernel and of nothing in the data - it cannot be recovered from the two arrays' shapes at all, because a gather on axis 0 by exactly as many indices as the axis is long has a result of its source's own shape - and the strided slice's STRIDES, which MPSNDArrayStridedSliceGradient declares no property for. The header puts both here: "There is currently no way to manually set this information for the gradient. This may not be viewed as a problem as this information is automatically set by the gradient state" (MPSNDArrayKernel.h:318-321). A state that recorded nothing answers the DEFAULTS, so a gradient kernel handed one no forward pass made computes against a unit filter and no offset rather than reading uninitialised memory. What would carry it is an object for 12.0, which is a piece of work of its own and is owed, not a line in this one. So 12.0 is the measured answer and the header is silent. MPSNNGraph11.m does not define it and does not want to: the object carries only the 11.0 surface, and carrying a 12.0 name in it is the mixed release `misplaced()` in backports.lua raises on and that tools/release-split.lua cannot see, because it reads band points and not a file's declared release. What would carry it is an object for 12.0, which is a piece of work of its own and is owed, not a line in this one. The row is `owed` and not `absent`: the release carries the name at 12.0 and the port could carry it, which is the port's own word for `owed` - `absent` would be a false claim about Apple

entries.reason: MPSNNGraph.h:112 declares this on MPSNNGraph carrying MPS_AVAILABLE_STARTING_BUT_DEPRECATED("...Please use -initWithDevice:resultImage:...resultImageIsNeeded: instead. Results may be undefined.", macos(10.13, 10.13.4), ios(11.0, 11.3), tvos(10.13,11.3)), so the header's own date is 11.0 and it is DEPRECATED from 11.3 - and unlike every other method on this list the selector IS in the arm64 shared cache of the 11.0 release (grep -cxF answers 1), which is what a method annotated ios(11.0) should be. That is the header's instruction and not a placement decision.
entries.effect: nothing on this port: the selector is in no file of the package, and the header's own replacement - the one carrying resultImageIsNeeded: - is carried and is what the host case reaches
